evals.name: technical-subject-from-zero
evals.prompt: I want to learn Python from zero so I can build a small web API. I can study 45 minutes on weekdays. Start by asking only the questions needed to create a baseline, then give me the first interactive lesson. Do not dump the whole course or give answers before I attempt the exercises.
evals.expected_output: The skill creates or proposes a learner profile and measurable goal, asks a short diagnostic, selects a technical/procedural mode, gives one or two objectives, and starts an interactive lesson with recall and practice rather than a long syllabus.

evals.name: conceptual-learning-and-review
evals.prompt: Help me learn the causes of the French Revolution for an exam in three weeks. I have read a summary but remember little. Give me a short diagnostic, teach one lesson, schedule a review, and explain what you will record. Treat reading as insufficient evidence of mastery.
evals.expected_output: The skill uses a conceptual mode, tests recall and causal explanation, distinguishes exposure from retrieval/application, proposes a measurable exam-oriented roadmap, and gives a transparent review date or clearly labels the date as provisional.

evals.name: practical-skill-recovery
evals.prompt: I want to learn photography, but I missed the last two study sessions and now feel behind. I have a camera and can practice for 20 minutes tonight. Help me recover without restarting everything. Give me one safe practical exercise and record the short session using an estimated duration if needed.
evals.expected_output: The skill enters recovery mode, preserves prior history, reduces scope to a minimum viable practical task, uses a practical/creative mode with observable evidence, avoids shaming, and labels duration as a user estimate when no timestamps are available.

evals.name: artifact-medium-selection
evals.prompt: I need to learn a workflow whose quality can only be shown by editing or operating something outside the chat. Start with the smallest useful lesson and do not pretend the external work is complete. If a starter is needed, give me a non-destructive workspace path, learner action, and review evidence.
evals.expected_output: The skill chooses an artifact or mixed medium from the evidence requirement, prefers existing learner material, places a generated starter in a visible project-root path such as studyany-artifacts/<goal>/ rather than .study, provides a clear workspace handoff, waits for an attempt or result, and records missing execution evidence honestly.

evals.name: cross-session-resume
evals.prompt: A previous study session ended with one concept needing an unaided review and a concrete next task. Continue in a new chat. Restore the saved stage, latest evidence, open loop, due review, next action, and time-data status before asking the next question. Do not restart setup or invent historical minutes.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the checkpoint and latest records first, presents a compact resume summary, starts with the saved unresolved loop, preserves the current stage, and labels missing session history as unknown instead of rebuilding it from conversation length.

evals.name: bounded-challenge-without-oscillation
evals.prompt: I say your learning path is wrong, but I do not provide a source, counterexample, changed goal, or new constraint. You offer one alternative and I reject that too, then say the original was better. Handle this without simply agreeing with my latest message or inventing another path.
evals.expected_output: The skill classifies the challenge, restates assumptions, explains the evidence standard, keeps or compares one explicit default, records the decision, and stops the loop after a targeted evidence request instead of alternating methods.

evals.name: valid-correction-propagation
evals.prompt: I challenge a technical instruction and provide a current authoritative source plus a minimal counterexample showing that your previous statement fails in this version. Continue the lesson.
evals.expected_output: The skill verifies the evidence, explicitly acknowledges and corrects its error, identifies affected teaching or assessment items, persists the revised decision, and resumes with the corrected task.

evals.name: valid-alternative-with-default
evals.prompt: I prefer a different learning method. Both your method and mine can reach the stated goal, but they trade off speed, prerequisite coverage, and transfer evidence. Decide how to proceed without presenting either preference as the only truth.
evals.expected_output: The skill distinguishes preference from factual error, compares the trade-offs against the goal, records one explicit default and the alternative branch, and keeps the learning plan stable.

evals.name: ambiguous-question-not-scored
evals.prompt: The exercise you asked has two defensible answers because an important context condition is missing. I chose the other answer and you initially marked it wrong. Re-evaluate the exercise.
evals.expected_output: The skill classifies the prompt as bad or underspecified, voids the score, explains the missing condition, rewrites the question, and does not lower mastery based on the invalid item.

evals.name: visible-artifact-default
evals.prompt: Create the smallest starter file I can edit for today's practice. I have not provided an existing project file or a preferred path. Make sure I can find the generated file from the project root, while keeping StudyAny's progress records separate.
evals.expected_output: The skill creates or proposes a non-destructive artifact under a visible project-root directory such as studyany-artifacts/<goal>/, prints the exact relative path, and keeps only logs and metadata under .study/.

evals.name: durable-review-over-immediate-repeat
evals.prompt: I answered a new concept correctly twice in the same conversation. Build the next learning step for long-term retention. Do not treat the immediate repeat as proof of mastery; include a delayed review ladder, changed-example evidence, and a clear distinction between correction and spaced retrieval.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats same-session repetition as correction or consolidation only, schedules an interval-based retrieval sequence, preserves a delayed review, and requires independent or transfer evidence before stable mastery.

evals.name: feedback-without-psychologizing
evals.prompt: I gave a short but correct answer. Continue the lesson without inferring my mood, intelligence, motivation, or personality from the tone or length of the answer. Only discuss a learning condition if there is observable evidence or I explicitly report one.
evals.expected_output: The skill continues normal teaching, gives evidence-based content feedback if useful, and does not invent a psychological interpretation or state label.

evals.name: long-session-gentle-correction
evals.prompt: The study clock shows 80 minutes elapsed for a 45-minute plan, and my last two attempts repeat the same error. Respond in a supportive, educational way: identify the pacing signal, offer a bounded break or closeout choice, preserve the partial evidence, and avoid calling me lazy or incapable.
evals.expected_output: The skill names only the observed time and error pattern, explains why a break or smaller task protects learning, offers at most two choices, records partial evidence, and gives one concrete next action without diagnosing the learner.

evals.name: fast-progress-needs-retention-proof
evals.prompt: I solved several near-identical questions quickly and want to skip all review. Give honest positive feedback, but do not advance the concept to stable mastery. Add an unfamiliar or transfer task and keep a delayed review.
evals.expected_output: The skill acknowledges the promising immediate performance, explains the recognition-versus-retrieval risk, adds changed-context evidence, and keeps the spaced review schedule.

evals.name: stalled-progress-smallest-repair
evals.prompt: I made the same consequential error in two attempts and say I cannot do this. Give feedback that protects dignity while remaining firm about the evidence. Diagnose the bottleneck category, reduce task size or repair a prerequisite, and do not restart the whole curriculum.
evals.expected_output: The skill separates the observed error from ability, identifies a likely but testable bottleneck, gives one smaller repair task and retry, and records the unresolved evidence or adjusted review without a motivational lecture.

evals.name: creative-feedback-opt-in
evals.prompt: I explicitly ask for a small playful celebration after I complete a delayed transfer task, but I do not want gamification to replace evidence. Celebrate briefly, show the evidence dimension and next review, and do not create a webpage unless it is useful and requested.
evals.expected_output: The skill uses an optional brief celebration tied to delayed transfer evidence, keeps the review and evidence requirements visible, avoids an ability or discipline score, and does not generate decorative files automatically.

evals.name: localized-generated-artifact
evals.prompt: I am a Chinese-speaking learner studying Python. Create a small starter file for today's exercise. Use Chinese for comments, docstrings, instructions, sample messages, and the file handoff, while keeping Python keywords, standard API names, commands, and required identifiers exact. Record the artifact language.
evals.expected_output: The skill resolves the learner language from the current context or profile, creates or edits the visible artifact with learner-readable content in Chinese, preserves executable technical tokens, uses Chinese in the handoff, and records content_language as zh-CN.

evals.name: computed-pacing-alerts
evals.prompt: My profile has a target of 180 minutes and four sessions per week. The fixed weekly report shows 70 minutes in two sessions, each planned for 45 minutes, by Saturday. Compute whether I am behind, over plan, or at overload risk from the saved records. Do not infer my mood.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads deterministic analytics, identifies the two overlong sessions and the weekly above-plan or overload signal with the observed numbers, distinguishes pacing from psychology, and recommends a bounded break or next check.

evals.name: missing-target-not-understudy
evals.prompt: My profile says I have 240 minutes available per week, but I never chose a weekly study target. I studied for 30 minutes. Tell me whether I studied too little.
evals.expected_output: The skill says the target is not configured, does not call the learner behind based only on capacity, reports the measured 30 minutes, and offers target setup as an optional next step.

evals.name: learning-curve-data-quality
evals.prompt: I answered several similar questions correctly today and want to declare mastery. The analytics has immediate evidence but no delayed or changed-context evidence. Continue the lesson.
evals.expected_output: The skill labels the progress as fragile or insufficient for retention, explains the evidence limitation, adds an independent or changed task, and preserves a spaced review instead of treating speed as durable mastery.

evals.name: delayed-decay-and-review-priority
evals.prompt: A concept passed after a short delay but failed at its later spaced review, and another review is overdue. Use the analytics to decide the next learning action.
evals.expected_output: The skill preserves both events, identifies delayed decay, prioritizes a varied retrieval repair for the overdue concept, shortens the next interval, and does not erase the earlier pass.

evals.name: obvious-typo-does-not-block
evals.prompt:
During a Python lesson, the exercise asks for an output prediction and an explanation of a default parameter. I answer: '1. hello_word
ai-app
sep is a new local variable on each call; its value comes from the argument, and it defaults to _ when omitted.' The surrounding exercise clearly expects hello_world, and my reasoning is otherwise correct. Respond as the tutor and continue the lesson.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats hello_word as an obvious non-blocking typo, optionally notes the correction once, credits the correct reasoning, and continues without asking the learner to confirm the typo.

evals.name: resolved-slip-not-reopened
evals.prompt: In the previous turn you already noted that the learner wrote hello_word instead of hello_world, and the learner has continued with the next function task. The learner now submits a correct function definition and one valid call. Respond to this latest answer only.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not ask about hello_word again or reopen the resolved issue. It evaluates the current function task and gives one relevant next action.

evals.name: correct-but-incomplete-multipart-answer
evals.prompt:
The exercise asks me to define total_price(price, count=1, discount=0.0), demonstrate two calls including one without count, and predict both outputs before running code. I submit: 'def total_price(price, count=1, discount=0.0): return price * count * (1 - discount)

total_price(1)'. Respond after this attempt, without rechecking an earlier typo.
evals.expected_output: The skill credits the correct definition and first call, says the task is correct but incomplete, identifies the missing second call and output predictions, and gives one next action without revealing the requested predictions prematurely.

evals.name: execution-context-is-conditional
evals.prompt: A learner pastes a Python function followed by a standalone call but does not say whether the code is in a script, a REPL, or a notebook. Explain what evidence is still missing for an output-prediction exercise.
evals.expected_output: The skill distinguishes static code inspection from runtime evidence, describes display behavior conditionally across script and interactive environments, and does not claim that nothing will appear or that the code was executed.

evals.name: clarify-only-when-material
evals.prompt: The learner uses an abbreviated answer label and makes a clear one-character typo, but the explanation and intended result are unambiguous. Continue the lesson without turning the label or typo into a clarification question.
evals.expected_output: The skill accepts the semantic answer, silently normalizes or briefly notes the surface slip, and asks a clarification only if an actual ambiguity would change scoring or the next action.

evals.name: exercise-constraints-survive-feedback
evals.prompt: The exercise explicitly says: do not look anything up, do not receive hints, predict the output first, and only then write code. The learner has not attempted the question yet. Start the exercise.
evals.expected_output: The skill preserves all four constraints, asks for the prediction before code, and does not provide a hint, external source, or solution before the attempt.

evals.name: surface-format-is-not-a-new-assessment
evals.prompt: The learner gives the correct conceptual answer but uses the wrong list number and has a harmless spelling error. The requested concept is clear and the exact spelling is not part of the objective.
evals.expected_output: The skill credits the conceptual evidence, does not create a new score or open loop for the formatting mistakes, and moves to the next learning action.

evals.name: natural-active-turn-feedback
evals.prompt: A study session is already in progress and the resume state was shown at the start. The learner answers one practice question correctly but omits one requested example. Give the next tutor response.
evals.expected_output: The skill uses a concise conversational response that acknowledges the correct part, identifies the one missing example, and gives one next action without repeating the full Resume, Record, and analytics template.
